newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - LONDON EVENING STANDARD - APRIL 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - LONDON EVENING STANDARD - APRIL 18.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Prime minister John Major is expected to announce an honours list later today, all those named will either be former ministers or senior politicians. The list will be the first published during an election campaign since 1970.
JARDINE FLEMING MAN IN MERCENARY PROBE

Rupert McCowan, an executive director at Jardine Fleming's Hong Kong corporate finance department has been suspended, amid allegations that he acted as a go-between the government of Papua New Guinea and a group of mercenaries known as Sandline International.

Eisuke Sakakibara, Japan's Finance Ministry chief has announced that Japan's economy is doing better than expected with its fiscal growth expected to exceed 2 per cent this year. Following the news the dollar fell against the yen today.
APPLE LOOKS FOR FRIENDLY BUYER AS LOSSES ROLL IN

Following a 27 percent drop in sales in the first three months of the year to 1.6 billion stg, Apple Computer have called in Goldman Sachs to 'review a number of investment proposals'. Ostensibly Apple are looking for a friendly buyer for the crisis-hit personal computer company.
SKY-HIGH LAND DEAL SETS A 938 MLN STG RECORD IN HK

Last month saw the remarkable purchase by Sino Land controlled by the Ng family of Singapore, of a record land deal. Chairman Robert Ng bid HK11.82 billion dollars (938 million stg) for a plot of 275,000 square feet.
